title: Can you afford to study in Europe? A Filipino’s guide to scholarships, costs
summary: From Erasmus+ scholarships and tuition grants to choosing budget-friendly university cities and navigating healthcare, here is what Filipino students need to know about studying in Europe

items: The European Higher Education Fair (EHEF) Philippines 2026 provides an opportunity for students to explore academic programs, tuition, and scholarships from 51 European universities, with a focus on affordability and living costs in different cities.

Studying abroad offers benefits beyond academics, such as exposure to diverse cultures and perspectives, while the EU aims to strengthen partnerships with Philippine institutions through student exchanges and collaborative programs.

MANILA, Philippines – Eighty-five Filipino students have been accepted into the European Union’s (EU) Erasmus+ program in 2026, adding to the 364 Filipinos awarded Erasmus Mundus scholarships between 2021 and 2025, as interest in European higher education continues to grow.

The figures, shared by Agata Nowicka, deputy head of mission of the delegation of the European Union to the Philippines, point to expanding opportunities for Filipinos seeking to pursue higher education in Europe.
However, choosing where to study also means considering tuition, living costs, admission requirements, and healthcare arrangements.
For students considering the move, the choice of destination can make a significant difference to their budgets.

In Spain, for example, studying in smaller cities such as Granada and Santiago can be considerably cheaper than living in Madrid or Barcelona, according to Alberto Tello, education advisor at the Embassy of Spain in the Philippines.

For Filipinos weighing their options, the European Higher Education Fair (EHEF) Philippines 2026 can provide an opportunity to explore these choices and get information directly from universities. The fair, held until Saturday, November 21, at Robinsons Manila, allows prospective students to compare academic programs, ask about tuition and scholarships, and learn about admission requirements. Online sessions are scheduled for November 23-25.
The event brings together 51 European universities, 34 of which are participating onsite. They represent 13 EU member states and are joined by 23 Philippine partner institutions.
The cost of studying abroad depends not only on tuition fees but also on where students choose to live.

In Spain, major cities such as Madrid and Barcelona tend to have higher accommodation, transportation, and everyday expenses. Tello pointed to alternatives where students can find a wide range of academic programs at lower living costs.
“I can think about cities like in South Granada, in North Santiago, where you can study everything, and everything is probably way, way cheaper,” Tello told Rappler.
Spain has approximately 90 universities, offering courses across different fields, although the availability of programs and costs vary by institution.

Filipino students can also apply for government scholarships to attend public universities. According to Tello, these grants can cover tuition fees, while scholarships at private institutions may offer additional support, including accommodation, depending on the applicant’s financial circumstances.

Healthcare is another consideration when calculating the cost of living abroad. Tello said foreign residents in Spain, including eligible students holding valid residence permits, can access the country’s public healthcare system.
This can reduce the need for separate private health insurance, although students should check the specific healthcare and insurance requirements attached to their visa and residency arrangements.

Interest in European higher education has grown, with 364 Filipino students receiving Erasmus Mundus scholarships between 2021 and 2025, compared with 320 during the preceding six-year period from 2014 to 2020.
Another 85 Filipinos have been accepted into the Erasmus+ program in 2026, according to Nowicka. The figure remains subject to change as the year’s program activities continue.
Nowicka said the application process has not necessarily become more restrictive, but the program has become more professional as organizers improve their selection procedures and implementation.

Eligibility depends on the specific opportunity. Some programs are intended for graduates seeking master’s degrees, while others require applicants to be enrolled at universities that collaborate with European institutions.

The Erasmus Mundus program, in particular, supports students pursuing joint master’s degrees offered by European universities, giving participants the opportunity to study in different countries during their academic journey.

Spain, Poland, and Ireland are among the destinations attracting questions from Filipino students, Nowicka said. She cited the availability of English-language programs and historical connections between the Philippines and some European countries as possible factors influencing students’ choices.

The participating institutions will provide information on postgraduate programs, admission requirements, tuition fees, scholarships, research opportunities, and student life.

This year’s fair also introduces changes intended to make it easier for Filipino students and universities to establish connections. European universities participating in online seminars have been paired with Philippine institutions to encourage longer-term academic partnerships.
Universities are also being presented by country, allowing prospective students to compare the educational opportunities available in each destination.
For students who pursue international education, the benefits can extend beyond academic qualifications.
Nowicka said studying abroad exposes students to different cultures and perspectives, helping them develop confidence and experience that they can bring back to their communities.
The EU also hopes that stronger university partnerships will lead to more joint research projects, academic exchanges, and collaborative programs between European and Philippine institutions.
The EU’s cooperation with the Philippines includes commitments to student and staff exchanges under the Enhanced Partnership launched in July 2026.
For prospective applicants, the immediate challenge is identifying a program that matches their academic background, financial resources, and long-term goals.
Comparing destinations, understanding scholarship eligibility, and accounting for living expenses are important steps before committing to a university abroad. – Rappler.com
